purpose: Self-contained retrieval cards distilled from the BA learning repository. Use these cards before drafting or reviewing BA artifacts.

cards.title: Elicitation and Stakeholder Discovery
cards.summary: Use elicitation to turn stakeholder statements into pain points, needs, constraints, assumptions, business rules, and candidate requirements.
use_when: A BRD/SRS is requested without enough context
questions: What business problem triggered this change?
Who owns the decision and who is affected by the change?
What happens today, step by step, including exceptions?
What pain is measurable: time, cost, error rate, risk, revenue, compliance?
What constraints are fixed: budget, deadline, policy, system, data, vendor?
quality_checks: Every pain point has an affected stakeholder
Every assumption has a validation owner
Every decision has an owner and date

cards.title: Product Vision and Project Classification
cards.summary: Before recommending BRD/SRS/backlog documents, classify the initiative. New products, platforms, SaaS/apps, B2B offerings, and commercializable MVPs require Product Vision before Project Charter and BRD.
use_when: MVP has a future product roadmap
User asks what documents are needed
questions: Is this an internal project only, or will it become a commercial product?
Who is the buyer and who is the daily user?
What problem should the product own better than current alternatives?
What is the 1-3 year direction beyond the first MVP?
Which document layer is needed first: Product, Business, Process, Requirement, UX, AI/Data, Technical, QA/UAT, or Delivery?
quality_checks: Product Vision is not replaced by BRD or Project Charter
Commercialization signal is explicitly checked
Target user and buyer are separated when different
Differentiator and success metrics are stated

cards.title: Business Requirements Document
cards.summary: BRD captures why the business needs change, what value is expected, and which business requirements are in scope before solution details are frozen.
use_when: Business goals and success metrics must be aligned
quality_checks: No feature without business need
Every BRQ is testable at business level
Scope boundary is explicit
Success metric has baseline and target when possible
cards.traceability: BRQ-* must map to FR-* or an explicit deferred/out-of-scope decision.

cards.title: Software Requirements Specification
cards.summary: SRS turns business requirements into implementable and testable functional/NFR/data/integration specifications.
use_when: Integration, data, and edge cases matter
quality_checks: Requirement is atomic
Actor and trigger are clear
Expected result is observable
NFR has measurable metric
Exception flow is covered
cards.traceability: FR-* and NFR-* must map back to BRQ-* and forward to Feature/US/TC coverage.

cards.title: User Story and Acceptance Criteria
cards.summary: User stories express value in role-goal-benefit form and must include acceptance criteria that QC/UAT can execute.
cards.pattern: As a [role], I want [goal], so that [benefit].
quality_checks: INVEST is satisfied
AC uses Given-When-Then
Story is small enough for one sprint
Business value is explicit
cards.traceability: US-* must map to Feature and FR-*; every US-* needs one or more TC/UAT scenarios.

cards.title: UAT Plan and Requirements Traceability Matrix
cards.summary: UAT validates business acceptance, while RTM proves every requirement is covered through story and test evidence.
quality_checks: No orphan BRQ/FR/NFR
Every UAT scenario has expected result
NFR has test strategy or evidence
Sign-off owner is named
cards.traceability: BRQ-* -> FR-* -> Feature -> US-* -> TC-* is the preferred full chain.

cards.title: Process and Requirement Modeling
cards.summary: Choose diagrams by the question being answered, not by decoration. Text and diagram must share actors, rules, IDs, and exceptions.

diagram_selector.who_interacts: Use Case Diagram or Context Diagram

quality_checks: As-Is is separated from To-Be
Gateway rules are explicit
Exception flow is represented
Diagram IDs match document IDs

cards.title: Data, API, Reporting, and Technical BA
cards.summary: Technical BA work clarifies data ownership, integration contracts, reporting definitions, and measurable NFRs.
use_when: Data migration or governance is in scope
quality_checks: Every metric has formula
Every API error path is specified
Every sensitive data field has classification
NFR has measurable threshold

cards.title: Product, UX, Wireframe, and Analytics
cards.summary: Product BA connects persona, pain point, journey, hypothesis, flow, screen behavior, and success metrics.
quality_checks: Every feature has target user and value
Every screen has behavior, validation, and empty/error/loading states
Events map to funnel or success metric
Rollout and feedback loop are defined

cards.title: AI/ML Feature Specification
cards.summary: AI/ML BA work must describe model purpose, inputs, outputs, metrics, acceptable error, fallback, monitoring, and human review.
quality_checks: Metric is stakeholder-readable
Low confidence behavior is defined
Training/source data ownership is clear
Human override is available for high-risk decisions

cards.title: Outsource BA and Sign-off Discipline
cards.summary: Outsource BA requires formal scope, baseline, decision log, change control, acceptance evidence, and handover discipline.
quality_checks: Scope baseline is approved
Every CR has cost/schedule/scope impact
Meeting minutes capture decisions and owners
UAT sign-off maps to milestone
Handover checklist includes source, docs, env, KT, warranty

cards.title: Finance, Banking, Insurance, and Transaction Domains
cards.summary: Financial and insurance domains require lifecycle/state control, reconciliation, audit, privacy, approval, and exception handling.
use_when: Payment, wallet, banking, lending, insurance, claim, policy, premium
quality_checks: No transaction without state machine
No money movement without reconciliation
No claim/policy flow without exception path
Approval and audit owner are named

cards.title: Healthcare and Government Domains
cards.summary: Healthcare and public-sector projects require workflow validation, privacy, consent, compliance mapping, multi-level acceptance, and operational readiness.
quality_checks: Clinical workflow is reviewed by SME
Regulation maps to features
Acceptance has levels and evidence
Security and continuity requirements are measurable

cards.title: BABOK v3 Framework: BACCM, Knowledge Areas, Techniques
cards.summary: BABOK v3 defines 6 Knowledge Areas (28 tasks), the 6-concept BACCM, 4 requirement classifications, 6 underlying competencies, 5 perspectives and 50 techniques. Use it to choose techniques, check that an artifact covers Change/Need/Solution/Stakeholder/Value/Context, and to answer certification questions.
use_when: User asks which BA technique fits a situation
A BRD or Vision needs a BACCM sanity check
User asks how a BA-agent step maps to BABOK
questions: Which of Change, Need, Solution, Stakeholder, Value, Context is not answered yet?
Which Knowledge Area task is this activity?
Is the requirement business, stakeholder, solution (functional or non-functional) or transition?
Is the technique one of the 50 in BABOK v3 or a common practice outside it (Gap Analysis, Kano)?
quality_checks: Technique names match BABOK v3 chapter 10
Gap Analysis, Kano and Decision Tree are not presented as BABOK v3 techniques
Certification answers are checked against the official guide

cards.title: Strategy Analysis and Business Case Judgement
cards.summary: Reframe the problem apart from the solution, grade evidence E1-E4, compare at least 3 options (Do Nothing, a light option, a full option) with assumptions, break-even and sensitivity, and recommend with stop conditions.
use_when: ROI is requested without baseline data
questions: Does the problem statement contain a solution?
What is the evidence level of each current-state claim?
What must be true for the full option to break even?
Which assumption flips the conclusion if it changes by 30 percent?
quality_checks: Do Nothing is present
A light option without development is present
No invented numbers; assumptions are labeled

cards.title: Solution Evaluation and Benefit Realization
cards.summary: Write KPIs with baseline, denominator, data source, guardrail and a review schedule; check KPI sets for arithmetic consistency; decide keep, tune, extend or stop at day 90.
questions: What is the baseline and when was it measured?
What is the denominator?
What decision follows if the target is missed?
Which guardrail detects harm?
quality_checks: No KPI contradicts another (weekly vs monthly usage)
Every goal has a result metric and a guardrail

cards.title: Elicitation Playbook and Difficult Situations
cards.summary: Prepare hypotheses, ask for the last real case and exceptions, handle stakeholders who give solutions, rank everything Must, stay silent, or contradict each other, and send a play-back within 24 hours.
questions: What do I need to know by the end of this session?
Tell me about the last time this went wrong
Who decides if two departments disagree?
quality_checks: Each claim has an evidence level and a source
Open items are marked for confirmation

cards.title: Risk-Based Rigor Tiers
cards.summary: Score 7 risk questions to choose Tier 1, 2 or 3. Tier sets document depth, number of AC scenarios, review and scripts. Some rules never relax: fact/assumption split, AC per story, traceability to a need, AI-Drafted label, no sensitive data at Tier 1.
use_when: A rule seems excessive for a small feature
questions: Does it handle money, children, health, biometrics or legal sanctions?
Is any integration unconfirmed?
Is change after go-live expensive?
quality_checks: Relaxations are written with a reason
Tier is raised when sensitive data is found

cards.title: Senior BA Rubric and Semantic Cross-Check
cards.summary: Nine dimensions graded 1-3 (framing, evidence, options, conflict, rigor, requirement quality, communication, compliance, value measurement). Senior needs no dimension below 2 and at least six at 3. Seven semantic checks compare FR, US and AC beyond ID matching.
use_when: A scanner reports PASS but numbers may disagree
questions: Do the thresholds in FR and AC match?
Is any behavior in FR untested by AC?
Does any AC add a requirement the FR does not state?
quality_checks: Red flags lower the level by one
Evidence is quoted from the document

cards.title: Vietnam Regulatory Watchlist (unverified)
aliases: bảo vệ dữ liệu cá nhân
cards.summary: A list of Vietnamese legal topics to ask about when specifying systems (personal data, children, cybersecurity, e-transactions, e-invoice, AML/KYC, healthcare records, public procurement). Marked unverified; the BA routes questions to legal counsel and records confirmed sources and check dates.
use_when: A regulated domain is in scope
questions: Which text applies and who confirmed it?
What is the date of the last check?
output: Open Questions with owner and due date
quality_checks: No article numbers or penalties quoted from this list
Legal conclusions come from legal counsel
